parsed.draft: Hi Varun, good to meet at the meetup, and thanks for the docs. On your question — whether our agent can read your webhook events: [our answer]. Looking forward to the call on the ninth. Arjun

next_move.who: Arjun, with whoever can check the agent against Cleanwave's API docs
next_move.what: Check whether our agent can read Cleanwave's webhook events, and reply to Varun with the answer before the call.

facts.claim: Varun Iyer, founder of Cleanwave, wrote after meeting Arjun at a meetup, shared Cleanwave's API docs, and asked Arjun to confirm whether our agent can read Cleanwave's webhook events before they meet.
facts.quote: confirm whether your agent can read our webhook events before we meet?

facts.claim: Varun has booked a call for the ninth of October at four in the afternoon IST.
facts.quote: booked Thursday 9 Oct, 4 pm IST. Cheers, Varun

facts.claim: His question is open and waits on us.
No answer of ours to Varun is measured in the file.

inferences.claim: Varun wants the webhook answer before the call so the call can be spent on the integration, not on finding out whether it is possible.
The answer needs a technical check of Cleanwave's API docs against what our agent reads — Arjun's or the team's to give, not a scheduling note.

patterns.claim: The file is new — seen once, with no earlier card or outcome — so there is no record of how Cleanwave takes a late answer.

hypotheses.proposition: Our agent may read webhook events of this kind today.
hypotheses.needs: A look at Cleanwave's API docs against what the agent can read.

hypotheses.proposition: Varun may read a missing answer as a sign the integration is not ready.
hypotheses.needs: His tone at the call, or a chase before it.

unknowns.question: Can our agent read Cleanwave's webhook events today?
unknowns.relevance: It decides whether the reply is a yes, a not-yet with a plan, or a no — and what the call is for.

unknowns.question: Did Arjun give Varun an answer in person or on another channel?
unknowns.relevance: If so, the question is closed and only the call remains.

unknowns.question: Who from our side should join the call?
unknowns.relevance: A technical question may need an engineer on it.

frames.primary: A warm integration partner with a technical question waiting on us, due before the call he booked: can our agent read Cleanwave's webhook events?
rivals: A routine scheduling thread, where the call itself will settle the question.
An early sign of a poor fit: if the agent cannot read their events, the call becomes about whether to build it.

expected_vs_actual.expected: From the brief's goal of landing design partners and Varun's own words: the webhook question answered before the call, and the call spent on the integration.
expected_vs_actual.actual: The question is unanswered in the file, and the call is booked for the ninth of October.

scenarios.do_nothing: Varun comes to the call without his answer, its first part goes on the question he asked days before, and the partner reads the silence as a gap.
scenarios.act: A short answer before the call — yes, not yet, or no with what it would take — lets the call go straight to the integration.
scenarios.best: The agent reads their webhook events, Varun hears so before the call, and it ends with a design-partner next step.
scenarios.worst: No answer comes, the call opens on the question, and the agent turns out not to read their events — the partnership starts on the back foot.
signals_to_watch: A reply to Varun before the call
Varun writing again before the ninth
The call staying on the calendar or being moved

reasons: Landing design partners is a goal the brief names, and Cleanwave is one of the brief's design partner talks.
Varun asked for the answer before a call he booked on a fixed date.
A late or partial answer can be mended at the call, so a wrong move is cheap to reverse.

parsed.alternative: If the check cannot be finished in time, write to Varun before the call with what is known so far, and say the full answer comes at the call.
parsed.wait_or_stop: Nothing to wait for — the move is ours; once the answer is sent, the file waits for the call on the ninth.
parsed.done_when: Varun has our answer on the webhook events before the call, and the call goes ahead as booked.
